| narrator | 024119bfc4b951b0 | 9.0 s | The Atrapos sector was named by its first surveyors after Atropos - eldest of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who cuts the thread of every life. |
| narrator | 96539f773a39ec85 | 3.3 s | Pilots joke that out here, the thread is always short. |
| narrator | b301ee008e79cb36 | 9.8 s | For three nights now, every receiver in the sector has picked up the same faint signal: a slow spiral of symbols, repeating, from somewhere beyond the charted lanes. |
| radio | 130d83c92da9ed16 | 10.0 s | Kephala Outpost to any independent pilot: Dr. Ariadne Kephala requests assistance with the anomalous signal. Please dock at Kephala Outpost. Paying work. |
| ariadne | 96db1d99da7c0d23 | 8.4 s | Thank you for coming. I'm an archaeologist - Aegean Bronze Age, Crete mostly. Which is why this signal is keeping me awake. |
| ariadne | b07b7e00739e11dd | 7.9 s | It isn't noise. It's 45 distinct symbols, stamped out one by one in a spiral, read from the rim toward the centre. |
| ariadne | 6f74427dd4d8da72 | 14.1 s | That is exactly the structure of the Phaistos Disc - a clay disc found in a Minoan palace on Crete in 1908. 241 stamped signs, 45 different ones, spiralling on both faces. Nobody has ever read it. |
| ariadne | 4c38b219e80d6b60 | 5.7 s | I've triangulated the source to the east of here. I've marked it on your map. Please - go and look. |
| narrator | 5d844ff2d40a31f0 | 6.1 s | Something is drifting at the heart of the signal - small, reddish, turning slowly. It isn't metal. |
| ariadne | 19d49b9546ccbeae | 5.2 s | Wait, I'm reading other ships near you. Raiders - they're flying a red bull's head as their banner. |
| ariadne | 607a781e222ba74a | 3.1 s | They must have followed the signal too. Don't let them take it! |
| ariadne | cacef2c33a7cb486 | 2.9 s | The raiders are gone. Can you get close to that object? |
| ariadne | cbfcddbc6cf04f63 | 10.1 s | ...It's fired clay. A fragment of a disc, covered in stamped signs. Fired clay, floating in deep space. That's impossible. Bring it in, carefully. |
| ariadne | a5ba05ce634f7153 | 3.6 s | Come straight back to Kephala Outpost. I'll have the lab ready. |
| ariadne | a026049b9b50e01f | 7.9 s | Look at the edge of the fragment. This second band of signs isn't Phaistos-style at all. It's Linear A - the everyday script of the Minoans. |
| ariadne | 98a278a0c6ee41f6 | 12.3 s | Linear A has never been deciphered. The Mycenaean Greeks later adapted it into Linear B, and an English architect, Michael Ventris, cracked Linear B in 1952. But Linear A still keeps its secrets. |
| ariadne | b37e9f36c63d2fd8 | 7.7 s | Except - this fragment resonates. Feed it energy and the signs shift, like the disc is trying to teach us to read it. |
| ariadne | 1b9e41d4f82d35b5 | 9.4 s | I need a resonator: 4 Energy Cells to power it and 6 Titanium Ore for the frame. Wrecks carry cells; titanium comes from the blue-grey asteroids. |
| ariadne | e735f9b61fc024d0 | 6.6 s | It worked. The Linear A band is a list of places - star positions. Each one points to the next. |
| ariadne | eb2bcfaf182f8093 | 10.4 s | In the myth, Princess Ariadne of Crete gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could find his way out of the Labyrinth. This is a thread through the dark - and I'm afraid I'm going to name it after her. |
| ariadne | ad9e85538d17c44e | 3.7 s | The first point is north of Knossos Station. Follow the thread. |
| narrator | eeef1fa2aae106bb | 6.0 s | The beacon wakes as you arrive. A double-headed axe of light turns slowly above it - a labrys. |

| kilon | 711bb6f095695f5c | 8.5 s | Around us lies New Hellas: a collection of solar systems ruled by the great Hellenic empires, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. |

| kilon | d2c22c0609e3ed51 | 2.3 s | Where it leads now: Enter the heart of the Labyrinth. |
| kilon | 38802f343357b60d | 3.7 s | Where it leads now: Defeat the Minotaur, guardian of the Labyrinth. |
| kilon | 64dfe4e702e3e6e2 | 2.1 s | Where it leads now: The thread is complete. |
| kilon | 278820df0b969587 | 7.6 s | Sing, Muse, of the pilot who came to the city of grey-eyed Athena, when her olive withered and the sea rose against her people. |
| kilon | 2f8c31554c9a685f | 12.5 s | Long ago, men say, two gods strove for the land: Poseidon struck the rock with his trident and a salt spring leapt out; Athena planted an olive. The people chose the olive, and the city took her name. |
| daidalos | 73cd3433825bed0c | 7.0 s | Welcome, stranger. Sit, eat, and then tell me your name - so the custom of our fathers commands, and so I keep it. |
| daidalos | 5c859bf372316588 | 10.2 s | Hear our grief. The olive in the garden-ring of the Akropolis, grown from the seed of the goddess's own tree, is withering. Salt is in its roots, and no engineer can say how it came there. |
| daidalos | 9f6b5f6d2b59d20a | 9.8 s | When the wise do not know, the wise ask. Go to the silver mines of Laurion in the Marathon system. The priestess Diotima keeps the bronze owl there; it speaks with the voice of the goddess. |
| kilon | dfcbe144c732cda3 | 8.2 s | Laurion: a grey moon riddled with old shafts, where the city's silver was dug by men who never saw the sun. There the owl keeps its watch. |
| ariadne | e2a8a3b820214595 | 6.1 s | You come as the goddess said you would - unasked, and in a hurry. Sit. The owl does not speak to the hurried. |
| kilon | d3c390407aac83a7 | 9.0 s | The sea's lord was robbed and has not forgotten. Where the cape of Sounion faces the dawn, thieves drank from his altar. Find them, and the salt will leave the root. |
| ariadne | a8f9e4a8e7a64fac | 7.0 s | Sounion lies in the system of Athenai itself. The Sea Peoples have a den beyond our gates; it was they, surely. |
| kilon | feaa78b6d668fcf0 | 7.7 s | At Sounion the raiders sat round their fires like wolves round a felled stag, and the bronze trident of Poseidon lay among them, black with soot. |
| kilon | 4e41f45a0921c122 | 6.0 s | So the thieves fell, and the trident of the Earth-shaker lay in the pilot's hold - heavy as a guilty conscience. |
| daidalos | f82c498aa65ac540 | 10.0 s | You have the god's trident? Then do not keep it an hour longer than you must. Gods are not asked twice. Bring gifts with it to the harbour-shrine at Piraeus: oil, wine and bread, as our fathers did. |
| daidalos | cecb97dd2122eba2 | 4.8 s | Do not haggle over the gifts, pilot. A man who bargains with a god has already lost. |
| kilon | 05f103843e97a8bc | 7.3 s | They poured the wine on the deck of the harbour-shrine and burned the bread, and the smoke went up to the dark between the stars. |
| daidalos | c45fb1a11a3a5a8e | 7.2 s | The Earth-shaker has his trident and his gifts. Now set the trident back where it was taken, on the cape of Sounion, and say his name as you do it. |
| kilon | 3a2c703b332bcead | 7.4 s | Then the pilot turned the ship back towards Sounion, carrying the god's own weapon through the god's own sea. |
| kilon | dbf7757038f166e0 | 10.3 s | The trident was set in its place, and the pilot said the god's name. Far off, the gates of Athenai flickered once, as if a wave had passed through them, and were still. |
| daidalos | 1e045ada72a24841 | 8.3 s | The salt is leaving the roots! But listen - the Sea Peoples have heard who robbed them of their prize. Their ships gather beyond Piraeus to burn our harbour. |
| kilon | 2eef372cfc6ba95b | 6.8 s | In Piraeus the ships lay side by side like spears in a rack, and their crews sharpened their weapons and said little. |
| daidalos | 877f61d34ede5d35 | 9.5 s | They are many and we are few. So we will not meet them in open space. We will meet them in the narrows before the gate to Ugarit, where their numbers are a burden and not a strength. |
| daidalos | b8cc6f2e1847626d | 6.2 s | An oracle once told our fathers to trust in wooden walls. Our walls are hulls now. Yours is one of them. |
| kilon | 8edd015f6850a92b | 7.2 s | As starlings wheel over a field before rain, so the raiders came through the gate, wheeling and crying on their radios. |
| daidalos | 65fd48fd75e365e1 | 5.4 s | Their van is broken. But see - their great ships come behind, and their chief with them. Do not let them pass. |
| radio | 9dfa79e8f79d909f | 4.0 s | Owl-folk! I will hang your ships from my mast like a fisher hangs his catch! |
| kilon | eb0b310646418eaa | 6.9 s | So the chief fell in the narrows, and the sea of stars was strewn with wrecks as a beach is strewn with weed after a storm. |
| daidalos | 3b2abefb6769ed7e | 8.2 s | Victory! Now the city must hear it before rumour reaches it first - rumour is quicker than any ship. Run, pilot, to the Stoa at Athenai, and do not stop. |
| kilon | 047325f46eac1bc1 | 8.7 s | Once a runner ran from Marathon to the city with news of victory, spoke one word, and died. The pilot flew, and hoped for a kinder ending. |
| daidalos | 78e92252f7513f3a | 4.3 s | Rejoice - we have won! You came faster than the rumour. The city will remember it. |
| daidalos | 97ed5c922dc3d91e | 5.7 s | Rumour came before you, pilot, but it told the truth this once. No matter - you are here, and alive. |
| kilon | cfd25595f2098385 | 7.5 s | That day the people walked in procession round the Akropolis-ring, as at the great festival, and carried a new robe to the goddess. |
| daidalos | 8de063a9e6e81233 | 8.7 s | And look: the olive puts out new leaves. Grey-eyed Athena has seen it all. Take this, and take the city's thanks - you are a guest-friend of Athens, now and always. |
| kilon | 06fc7329139c62a3 | 8.5 s | Sing, Muse, of Lakedaimon, the hollow land, whose people spend few words and many years of training - and of the stranger who stood among them. |
| ariadne | 0fbc469172922f46 | 5.1 s | You. Pilot. We have a task. We do not give tasks to men we have not tested. |
| ariadne | c7416a985d32b272 | 4.8 s | Raiders prowl the gate to Pylos. Three of them. Go alone. Come back. |
| kilon | 7b59fe8c2338c8d8 | 6.7 s | When a king of Macedon wrote to them, 'If I enter your land I will destroy you,' the Spartans answered with one word: 'If.' |
| kilon | 4351c9b3f3e5f9cb | 9.8 s | Spartan boys were sent out alone, with no shoes and one cloak, to live by their wits. The ephor asked the stranger for less than that - and watched closely all the same. |
| ariadne | a943cacc0e279a95 | 0.7 s | Good. |
| ariadne | 20bd83a960001dee | 7.2 s | Now the real task. Go to the shrine at Amyklai. The priest has an answer from Delphi. We do not like it. |
| ariadne | 280b7114734283a6 | 6.3 s | Amyklai. The shrine of Apollo, where Hyakinthos died. Listen to the priest. Speak little. |
| daidalos | 9dc9870c1cd225e9 | 7.2 s | Far-shooting Apollo gave this answer to our kings long ago, and gives it again: 'Love of money, and nothing else, will destroy Sparta.' |
| daidalos | 56e72a4772c12119 | 12.4 s | Now hear what the god did not say, but we know. Leotychidas, once our polemarch, was sent into exile for taking a bribe. He has sold the codes of the Thermopylai gate to the Sea Peoples for a sleeve full of gold. |
| daidalos | cd9d06b249c546d5 | 6.1 s | The garrison at Thermopylai Citadel must hold the pass. They are few. They are hungry. Bring them what they need. |
| kilon | 0992c32f0434d853 | 9.2 s | Thermopylai: the hot gates. A narrow way between the mountains and the sea, where a few may hold back many - if they are fed, and armed, and do not run. |
| daidalos | 0fc60e545279777f | 2.9 s | Bread and spears. Good. Now we can fight. |
| daidalos | 68dd87bcec3ff933 | 6.9 s | A merchant told me their ships will be so many that their guns will hide the stars. Then we shall fight in the shade. Take your place at the gate to Lukka. |
| kilon | d5f5e9571b3de06e | 5.7 s | They came through the narrow gate as a river comes through a gorge, and the Spartans stood in it like rocks. |
| daidalos | 55ae703b19731948 | 3.3 s | First wave broken. They will send more. They always do. |
| daidalos | 987617bd4f1fee71 | 4.6 s | There. The traitor's ship. He comes himself, to see what his gold has bought. |
| radio | 455f2961ce10a5bf | 5.0 s | Spartans! I offer you what I was offered - gold, and your lives. Stand aside. |
| kilon | b3f4bfb859d080fa | 5.3 s | The gold in his sleeve did not save him. It never does; that was the meaning of the god's answer. |
| daidalos | 412b128bb21b8fed | 9.6 s | The pass holds. Now the Twin Stars. Kastor and Polydeukes, sons of Zeus, guard every sailor - their beacons at the Kastor Phalanx went dark when the raiders came. Relight them. |
| kilon | 63b73273a690e386 | 7.6 s | Two stars, side by side, that sailors look for when the storm is worst. Their beacons had gone out the night the traitor's raiders came. |
| kilon | a621c6ef7c3993d3 | 8.9 s | When the Twin Stars burn on a ship's mast, sailors say, the storm is over. The pilot set them burning again, and every ship in the lanes saw them. |
| ariadne | 56aa53e29492c1b1 | 12.9 s | Bad news. At Tainaron, where the road to Hades opens, the three-headed hound has broken out. Herakles, father of our kings, dragged it up from below once. Now it is your turn. |
| kilon | e64ed494eb9223f8 | 6.5 s | Three heads it had, and a mane of snakes, and its bark shook the hulls of ships as the bark of a dog shakes a sleeping house. |
| kilon | c3ac3d519daa7670 | 5.2 s | So the hound of Hades went back down the road it came, and the gate of Tainaron was shut. |
| ariadne | 1ea983772eea8274 | 2.4 s | Come back. Report. Keep it short. |
| ariadne | 6fe85081b251f830 | 6.7 s | A Spartan mother tells her son, as she hands him his shield: 'With it, or on it.' You came back with yours. |
| ariadne | 3f9ef4ea003dbc38 | 4.4 s | Take this. Few strangers are called friends of Lakedaimon. You are. |
| kilon | 204720b69e0b4889 | 9.1 s | Sing, Muse, of Mykenai rich in gold, of its walls that the Cyclopes built, and of the curse that runs in its kings' blood like rust in a blade. |
| daidalos | 30d0c2d61521d91f | 7.1 s | Stranger, you stand in the hall of the wanax. Drink from my cup - and then hear me, for the gods have turned their faces from my house. |
| daidalos | 0a509b8f817776f2 | 6.9 s | The golden mask of my fathers was taken from the tholos-tomb, and the next night the Lion Gate's beacon went dark, and the great walls cracked. |
| daidalos | d01e0c4fd60db20a | 7.8 s | Old Brontes, last of the Cyclops-engines, still tends the forge at Tiryns. He built these walls. Ask him what has broken them. |
| kilon | 11d51870761b56ff | 7.4 s | Tiryns of the great walls: there the Cyclops-engine still beats its anvil, slow as a heart, as it has since the days of Perseus. |
| asterion | e786675712fa346d | 9.7 s | One eye I have, and with it I have watched three thousand years. Walls do not crack by themselves, little one. A thief opened the tomb, and the dead were angry. |
| asterion | 683e075142a47127 | 7.8 s | First mend the walls. Bring iron and titanium to the forge at the Lion Gate of Tirynthia, and I will set the stones as I set them for Perseus. |

| asterion | 0079fcae0c37d817 | 6.5 s | The thieves took the mask towards the den of Lukka. Their sentries watch the gate from Mykenai. Clear the road. |
| kilon | c9eb36edc9879026 | 5.1 s | The pass to Lukka: where the raiders watch, as crows watch a field from the top of a dead tree. |
| daidalos | 111604a820e351f9 | 8.5 s | The road is open. But a worse thing stirs. In the marsh of Lerna, beside our own world, the many-headed serpent that Herakles killed has grown its heads again. |
| daidalos | cc40322665d56d43 | 4.9 s | Herakles cut one head and two grew in its place. Do not be proud, pilot. Be patient. |
| kilon | 533a19db3f83a1d9 | 4.8 s | Nine heads it had, and its breath was poison, and the marsh boiled where it moved. |
| kilon | 3bc80c21b328de68 | 5.8 s | So the Hydra died a second time; and the pilot did not boast of it, remembering what happens to the proud. |
| daidalos | e060539eaa0cc8d0 | 7.5 s | Now we sail to take back the mask. But the fleet cannot jump. The gates are still, as the winds were still at Aulis when Artemis was wronged. |
| daidalos | d16bfb306fee2c5d | 6.3 s | Kalchas sees what was, what is and what will be. He has never told a king good news. Go and hear him anyway. |
| daidalos | ef5c683517409627 | 7.2 s | Artemis is angry. One of the wanax's captains shot a hind in her sacred grove and boasted that not even the goddess could shoot better. |
| daidalos | 888cc85a9e5a62d0 | 10.1 s | Once, at Aulis, she asked for a king's daughter. But in the better telling she took a hind instead, and carried the girl away to safety. Give her gifts of healing and clean water, and she will be content. |
| daidalos | 4caaf928e47d7c3a | 6.7 s | Medicine for her healing hands, water for her clean springs. Artemis loves the wild things, and those who keep them whole. |

| daidalos | eb42a4457fd0f092 | 10.0 s | Bring it home - but beware the sea between. Once Poseidon sent a monster, Cetus, against the land of Andromeda, until Perseus of our house killed it. My dreams say it is out again. |

| daidalos | 8a1d94b2f5846a0f | 11.2 s | Know this, guest: my house has a curse on it, from the day Atreus served his brother a terrible feast. Each king pays for the pride of the one before. You have bought us a little peace. Take gold for it - but take my friendship more. |
| kilon | d6d4ad578cc79e50 | 6.7 s | Sing, Muse, of Ionia, where men first asked not which god made the world, but what the world is made of. |
| daidalos | c97e9ef80a480969 | 7.8 s | Welcome, guest. I write down the stories of the Greeks - which are many, and, it seems to me, mostly foolish. Yours I would like to hear when it is finished. |
| daidalos | 9be825c425d26cd6 | 9.2 s | Thales of our city foretold an eclipse of the sun, and it came on the day he named. Now the observatories say another is coming - one that will blind the gate-beacons of the whole League for an hour. |
| daidalos | 49088f65212243b5 | 10.1 s | Worse: a raider named Herostratos boasts he will do a deed so great that men will speak his name for ever. Such men are dangerous. The League's council meets at the Panionion. Go and tell them. |

| daidalos | 74e48eab7e91f28b | 10.1 s | Twelve cities sit in this council, and twelve cities never agree. But on this we agree: Ephesos must be guarded, and the eclipse must be measured, so that the gates can be steered by hand while it lasts. |
| daidalos | 7ea6d9fc594260f7 | 7.5 s | Theano of Samos, who keeps the school of Pythagoras, is building the instrument. She needs parts. Bring them to the Sappho Observatory. |
| ariadne | 880fa4e522353c53 | 11.3 s | Pythagoras taught that all things are number: the strings of the lyre, the rings of the planets, even justice. This instrument hears the numbers of the sky, and will tell us the second the shadow falls. |
| ariadne | d5100e4dc96b9d29 | 6.2 s | Herostratos's scouts have been seen at Ephesos, by the strait. Drive them off before they learn too much. |
| ariadne | 468f4cbbeadaeee7 | 4.9 s | Be quick and be careful. A man who wants to be remembered will do anything to be noticed. |
| daidalos | a650b00593c563f9 | 11.1 s | The scouts carried fire-charges, the kind used to burn a station. Pilot - it is the temple of Artemis he means to burn. It is the greatest wonder of the League. Hurry to the temple-ring beside Ephesos Agora. |
| kilon | af48b642952ec865 | 10.4 s | The temple of Artemis at Ephesos had a hundred and twenty-seven columns, each the gift of a king. Its ring now shone in the dark beside the Agora like a crown laid on black cloth. |

| daidalos | d41163b35e3a4df9 | 5.4 s | The singer at the Odeon has asked for you. Singers do not usually ask - they are usually asked. Go. |
| daidalos | f23ede576b9fd5f7 | 9.8 s | Sit, guest. I am a singer, as my fathers were. I have made a new song - about a pilot, a burned temple that did not burn, and a monster that Odysseus could not kill. |
| daidalos | 2986dfb012dd4e3d | 9.4 s | What is everything made of? Thales said water, Anaximenes air, Herakleitos fire, Pythagoras number. I say: stories. Take the League's gold - the song is free. |
| kilon | 41274d3e734463e1 | 6.3 s | Sing, Muse, of the Isles that stand in a circle round holy Delos, as dancers stand round an altar. |

| ariadne | 7685bac0f9944797 | 13.7 s | Each pillar was made with a gift from one isle: Siphnos gave gold, Melos obsidian, Paros marble, Naxos the vine. We must gather the gifts again. Begin with Siphnos - and remember what happened to the Siphnians who cheated the god. |

| ariadne | 148765fe63dca5cf | 10.4 s | One rite remains. On Keros, the old people broke their marble figures and laid them down, all together, in one place. We still do. Bring the offering there. |
| kilon | da97dc6613bc94fa | 8.2 s | Keros: a small island where nobody lives, and where, for a thousand years, the people of the Isles came to break what they had made. |
| kilon | a0a080306af85a5f | 11.8 s | They broke the white figures with their folded arms and their quiet faces, and laid the pieces down together, as their fathers had for a thousand years. No one now knows why. Perhaps it does not matter. |
| ariadne | 72d7d8263d5b8963 | 6.4 s | The Isles are one circle again. Take our thanks, guest - and our gold, which is honest. |
| kilon | 36d0dc68e9a5c678 | 1.5 s | The thread is in your hands. |
